full_judgment: 12. On consideration of the submissions advanced on behalf of both the parties and on perusal of the impugned judgment and order and the materials on record it appears that, admittedly, the suit land belonged to Amarendra Nath and others. The plaintiffs of Title Suit No.31 of 20,09, (hereinafter mentioned as appellants claimed that Abdus Subhan Mia, (the plaintiff appellant No. l) and Abdul Hamid Hawlader (predecessor of Plaintiff appellant Nos. 2 to 6) took settlement of the suit land from Amarendra Nath and others; but they did not disclose the date or year of such settlement in their plaint. PW-1, Abdus Sobhan Miah, in his deposition stated that they took settlement from Baidhyanath in the year 1358 BS; but no other PW corroborated PW-1 in this respect nor has the settlement been proved by producing either Patta or Kabuliyat or any other written document. Under the Bengal Tenancy Act, though settlement may be granted orally without any written instrument but in case, if any question arose as to genuineness of such settlement then burden always lies upon the person claiming as such to prove the same settlement by proper oral evidence. But in the present case the appellants have failed to prove such settlement by any proper evidence either oral or documentary. Thus when the settlement, the basis of appellants title, is not proved by proper evidence, they cannot claim title through auction purchase.
